title: Composition design and performance of liquid low-reactivity mold fluxes for continuous casting of High-Mn High-Al steel
abstract:
Conventional powder mold fluxes used for the continuous casting of high-Mn high-Al steel are highly susceptible to aluminothermic reactions, which cause rapid compositional drift, increased viscosity, and unstable crystallization behavior. To address this problem, this study proposes a fluoride-free, low-reactivity liquid mold flux concept for a premelted liquid flux addition process. In this design strategy, the target is shifted from low-temperature melting performance to thermophysical stability in the 1350-1500 °C operating window. FactSage calculations were used to screen the CaO-Al2O3-BaO-(SiO2, B2O3, MgO, Li2O) system in terms of liquidus temperature and viscosity at 1350 °C, while thermodynamic considerations of reducible oxides were used to guide the control of steel-slag reactivity. Three representative compositions were then evaluated by static steel-slag reaction tests with a high-Mn high-Al experimental steel, high-temperature viscosity measurements, in situ CCT/TTT/DHTT crystallization analyses, and equilibrium precipitated-phase calculations.
                  The results indicate that, at fixed contents of 40 wt% CaO, 26 wt% Al2O3, 10 wt% BaO, and 4 wt% Li2O, a feasible low-reactivity composition window can be established by adjusting SiO2, B2O3, and MgO. Compared with conventional industrial reference mold fluxes, the designed liquid mold fluxes markedly suppressed Al and Mn oxidation and limited reaction-induced compositional drift. Among them, Slag-C exhibited the smallest Al2O3 enrichment after 40 min of steel-slag contact and maintained the most stable viscosity-temperature and crystallization characteristics. CCT/TTT/DHTT results further showed that the designed slags formed a more balanced liquid/crystalline/glassy film structure, while equilibrium calculations confirmed that the expansion of high-melting Al-rich phases after reaction was effectively restrained.
                  These findings demonstrate that liquid mold flux design for high-Mn high-Al steel should prioritize low steel-slag reactivity, viscosity stability, and moderate crystallization in a high-temperature steady-state window, rather than merely minimizing liquidus temperature. The proposed design framework provides a practical route for stable multi-heat continuous casting of high-Mn high-Al steel.
